rows.notes: The study is a global literature/document review (Section 3: systematic search of SEEA website, Scopus, Google Scholar; 271 water accounts from 139 publications catalogued in an Access database) proposing best-practice indicators. It reports no primary data, experiment, survey or model run of its own, so Q1 is no. It contains no result on a flow-metering network linked to a water-rights database for detecting illegal abstractions; the only related remark is a definitional note that SEEA treats apparent losses from illegal tapping and malfunctioning metering as part of water consumption (Section 5.2). The passage's specific claim about metering networks and water-rights databases is not something this review tests or reports.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a review/synthesis of water accounting practice, not a primary study; it does not address flow metering or social cohesion as technologies or effects.
